key_insight: Automatic differentiation reveals that aerodynamic information from sparse pressure probes is transported unevenly through compressible flow, creating localized regions where hidden parameters are most observable.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical framework for choosing informative sensor locations and improving inverse modeling of aerodynamic systems from limited pressure data.
method: Differentiate through a shock-capturing immersed-boundary flow solver.
Compute an observability metric from gradient sensitivity of pressure signals to unknown parameters.
Use inverse-learning tests to compare observability with actual parameter-recovery performance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports inverse-learning experiments across different flow regimes and airfoil geometries, showing that observability patterns and convergence behavior vary substantially.
watch_item: High observability does not always mean best parameter inference, so sensor selection should be validated with task-specific inverse-learning tests.
paper_title: Information Transport and Observability in Compressible Aerodynamics
